intent: One character position of an InputOtp, rendered as its own native input.
typical_uses: One character of a fixed-length code, inside an InputOtpGroup

dont_use_when.situation: A standalone text field outside an InputOtp, even a one-character one

invariants.text: A slot's position, and so which character of the root's value it shows and edits, is its render order among the root's slots; it takes no index prop. Typing a character moves focus to the next slot, and only the active slot is in the tab order.
Setting `aria-invalid="true"` on a slot tints its border and inset ring to the destructive color, and the invalid look wins over the focus ring while that slot is focused.

anti_patterns.dont: Render an InputOtpSlot outside any InputOtp
anti_patterns.do_instead: Mount it inside an InputOtpGroup under an InputOtp - the slot reads its character, its id and its disabled, read-only and masked state from the root through the primitive's context, and throws when that context is missing

a11y.by: The primitive's OTPField.Input (a real native input per slot, a roving tabindex that keeps only the active slot tabbable, aria-labelledby inherited from the root's label) plus input-otp.test.tsx's assertions that every slot is an INPUT element and that typing into the first slot moves focus to the second

render.states: render replaces the rendered element with one the caller supplies
render.because: Base UI's render prop takes an element or a function of the slot's own state, so its type is a union of a React element and a callback - neither expressible in JSON Schema.

style.states: style accepts a function of the slot's state as well as a plain style object
style.because: Base UI widens React's `CSSProperties` to `CSSProperties | ((state) => CSSProperties)` so a caller can style off the primitive's own state (filled, index, disabled, readOnly, ...). A JSON Schema `object` would reject the function form, so nothing is asserted; the kit's own styling goes through input-otp.module.css, not through this.

good.title: A slot marked invalid after a failed check

bad.title: An explicit slot index carried over from another OTP library
bad.why: InputOtpSlot declares no index prop, so tsc rejects it; the primitive derives each slot's position from render order instead.

render.description: TS: ReactElement<unknown, string | JSXElementConstructor<any>> | ComponentRenderFn<HTMLProps, OTPFieldInputState> | undefined. The compiler emits one JSON type per property; this type is left to tsc. render replaces the rendered element with one the caller supplies. Base UI's render prop takes an element or a function of the slot's own state, so its type is a union of a React element and a callback - neither expressible in JSON Schema.

style.description: TS: CSSProperties | ((state: OTPFieldInputState) => CSSProperties | undefined) | undefined. The compiler emits one JSON type per property; this type is left to tsc. style accepts a function of the slot's state as well as a plain style object. Base UI widens React's `CSSProperties` to `CSSProperties | ((state) => CSSProperties)` so a caller can style off the primitive's own state (filled, index, disabled, readOnly, ...). A JSON Schema `object` would reject the function form, so nothing is asserted; the kit's own styling goes through input-otp.module.css, not through this.
